# Model {#sec-model}

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd

rent = pd.read_csv("data/ACSDT5Y2024.B25064-Data.csv")
income = pd.read_csv("data/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013-Data.csv")
tracts = gpd.read_file("data/tl_2024_36_tract.zip")

rent = rent.iloc[1:].copy()
income = income.iloc[1:].copy()

rent["tract"] = rent["GEO_ID"].str[-6:]
income["tract"] = income["GEO_ID"].str[-6:]

rent["median_rent"] = pd.to_numeric(
    rent["B25064_001E"].astype(str).str.replace(",", ""),
    errors="coerce"
)
income["median_income"] = pd.to_numeric(
    income["B19013_001E"], errors="coerce"
)

data = rent[["tract", "median_rent"]].merge(
    income[["tract", "median_income"]],
    on="tract",
    how="inner"
)

tracts["tract"] = tracts["TRACTCE"]
```

## Rent and Income Relationship

This section examines the relationship between median household income and median gross rent across census tracts.

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
gdf = tracts.merge(data, on="tract", how="inner")
plt.scatter(gdf["median_income"], gdf["median_rent"])
plt.xlabel("Median Household Income")
plt.ylabel("Median Gross Rent")
plt.title("Median Income and Rent")
plt.show()
```

```{python}
import numpy as np

model_data = gdf[["median_income", "median_rent"]].dropna()

x = model_data["median_income"]
y = model_data["median_rent"]

slope, intercept = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
correlation = np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1]

print("Slope:", slope)
print("R-squared:", correlation ** 2)
plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.plot(x, slope * x + intercept)
plt.xlabel("Median Household Income")
plt.ylabel("Median Gross Rent")
plt.title("Median Income and Rent with Regression Line")
plt.show()
```

The results show a positive relationship between median household income and median gross rent. The R-squared value is about 0.21, which means income explains about 21% of the differences in rent across the census tracts.

## Rent Map

```{python}
gdf.plot(
    column="median_rent",
    legend=True,
    figsize=(10, 8)
)

plt.title("Median Gross Rent by Census Tract")
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()
```

The map shows differences in median gross rent across census tracts. Some areas have higher rents, while other areas have lower rents.

## Conclusion

The results show that areas with higher household income generally have higher rent. However, income does not explain all of the differences in rent.
